model.drift: zero by construction, not by sample average
model.increments: iid draws from the demeaned empirical return distribution

code.note: engine_version is static and identifies nothing on its own; commit is what names the code behind this artifact. dirty=true means tracked files differed from that commit when the run started, so the SHA locates the run but does not fully reproduce it. dirty=null means the run could not tell.

conventions.drift: Every model in this set is driftless: the engine's models and the null centre the pool they resample, and each challenger's simulated returns are centred before they are walked to prices. A model carrying drift scored against one denied it was worth up to +4.6% of spurious CRPS skill on this asset and that result was withdrawn; this is the guard against it reappearing six times over.
conventions.lookahead: none: each fit sees prices up to and including its as-of date
conventions.multiple_comparisons: Six models against one null at 5% finds a winner whether or not one exists. Hansen's SPA is the decision; the per-model Diebold-Mariano statistics are description. The Model Confidence Set answers the different question of which models cannot be excluded.
conventions.windows: One walk-forward, so every model was scored on the same as-of dates against the same realised outcomes. A date any model could not fit is a date none of them is scored on.

hansen_spa.null: no model in this set has a smaller expected CRPS than random_walk
hansen_spa.reading: One test over the whole set, so the multiplicity is inside the null distribution rather than corrected for afterwards. A loss differential here is benchmark minus model, so positive means the model lost less — the opposite of the Diebold-Mariano sign convention reported per model. best_model names the largest studentised differential and is a description of this sample, not a winner: where the p-value does not reject, no model in the set has been shown to beat the benchmark and the name should be read as noise.

model_confidence_set.reading: A set, not a ranking. It contains the best model with the stated probability, and on a sample this size it is usually large — which is the measurement rather than a failure of it. Models are listed in the order they were eliminated, each with the p-value of the test that removed it. A set containing every model means the sample cannot tell them apart.

non_overlapping_subsample.reading: The loss differential is crps_model - crps_null, so a negative statistic is the model losing less and a positive one is the model losing more. A large p-value means the skill score above is not distinguishable from zero on this sample, which is a statement about the evidence and not a demonstration that the two are equal.

overlapping_windows_hac.reading: The loss differential is crps_model - crps_null, so a negative statistic is the model losing less and a positive one is the model losing more. A large p-value means the skill score above is not distinguishable from zero on this sample, which is a statement about the evidence and not a demonstration that the two are equal.

diebold_mariano.status: description, not decision: read the SPA p-value for whether anything in this set beat the benchmark

minimum_detectable_effect.reading: The smallest true CRPS skill a Diebold-Mariano test on this sample would reject at, four times in five. It uses the loss-differential variance actually observed, the HAC lag the overlap implies and the same small-sample correction the test carries, so it describes the test that ran rather than an idealised one. A negative result above this number is evidence of absence; one below it is an absence of evidence, and the two are not the same finding.
